text: If you could restart your life tomorrow, what would you keep exactly as it is?
Send a message to someone you haven’t spoken to in over a year.
Most people wait for motivation before acting. The people who succeed act before motivation arrives.
Octopuses have three hearts and blue blood — and two of those hearts stop beating when they swim.
What are you tolerating today that your future self will wish you had changed?
The quality of your life is determined by the quality of your questions.
Who were you before the world told you who to be?
Spend one hour today with your phone in another room.
Honey found sealed in ancient Egyptian tombs is still perfectly edible after 3,000 years.
You don’t find time for what matters. You make it — and the making is the proof that it matters.
What would you attempt if you knew the attempt itself would change you?
We are what we repeatedly do.
author: Will Durant

text: What would you do differently if no one were watching?
When did you last do something for the first time?
What’s a belief you held five years ago that you no longer hold?
If you had to teach one thing you know to a stranger, what would it be?
What conversation have you been avoiding?
What would your life look like if you trusted yourself completely?
Notice the last time you felt fully present. What were you doing?
What’s something you’ve outgrown but haven’t let go of?
Where in your life are you choosing comfort over growth?
What would you tell yourself at the start of this year?
What’s the smallest thing that would make today better?
Who in your life deserves more of your attention than they’re getting?
What does ‘enough’ look like for you right now?
Write down three things you’re grateful for before you check your phone tomorrow.
Ask someone a question you actually want the answer to — and listen without planning your reply.
Do the task you’ve been postponing for fifteen minutes today, even imperfectly.
Compliment a stranger today, specifically and honestly.
Take a walk with no destination and no headphones.
Tell someone exactly how they helped you, even if it feels overdue.
Spend ten minutes today learning something with no practical use.
Say no to one thing today that you’d normally agree to out of habit.
Discipline is choosing between what you want now and what you want most.
Most regrets are not about what we did, but about what we never tried.
The questions you keep asking become the life you keep living.
Comfort and growth rarely share the same room.
The fastest way to feel behind is to compare your beginning to someone else’s middle.
What you tolerate, you teach the world to keep giving you.
A single bolt of lightning carries enough energy to toast about 100,000 slices of bread.
Bananas are botanically classified as berries — strawberries, surprisingly, are not.
The Eiffel Tower can grow more than six inches taller in summer from thermal expansion.
Wombat droppings are cube-shaped, which keeps them from rolling away and marks territory more effectively.
